cohort: Pregnant rats randomly allocated into four groups.
finding: Oral administration of horse chestnut extract in pregnant rats resulted in a substantial decrease in fetal weight, head diameter, tail diameter, and crown-rump length, and inhibited the formation of the central vein, portal area, and hepatic sinusoids, indicating teratogenicity.
birth_weight: Substantial decrease in fetal weight observed (fetuses extracted on day 18 of pregnancy).
gest_age: Exposure from day 0 to day 16 of pregnancy, effects estimated on day 18 of pregnancy (in rats).
